o: The apostle blesses God for his special benefits through Christ.
Salvation by Christ foretold in ancient prophecy.
All are exhorted to holy conversation.
Such as is suitable to their principles, privileges, and obligations.
bg: This epistle is addressed to "the strangers scattered abroad", i.e., to the Jews of the Dispersion (the Diaspora).
A province of Asia Minor, stretching along the southern coast of the Euxine Sea, corresponding nearly to the modern province of Trebizond. In the time of the apostles it was a Roman province.
The easternmost and the largest province of Asia Minor. Christianity very early penetrated into this country (1 Pet. 1:1).
"Simon was a Galilean, and he was that out and out...The Galileans had a marked character of their own. They had a reputation for an independence and energy which often ran out into turbulence.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle blesses God for his special benefits through Christ (vv. 1–9); Salvation by Christ foretold in ancient prophecy (vv. 10–12); All are exhorted to holy conversation (vv. 13–16); Such as is suitable to their principles, privileges, and obligations (vv. 17–25). People named: Peter. Places: Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, Bithynia.
ch.mh: This epistle is addressed to believers in general, who are strangers in every city or country where they live, and are scattered through the nations.
q: Read verses 1–9 (The apostle blesses God for his special benefits through Christ). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 10–12 (Salvation by Christ foretold in ancient prophecy), what do you learn about faith and trust?
Verse 22 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside 1 Timothy 1:5. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Peter’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of holiness in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 Peter?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: We should lodge it in our hearts as our only treasures here, and the certain pledge of the treasure of glory laid up for believers in heaven.
ch.a: Name one worry and deliberately hand it over to God in prayer each day this week.

o: A temper suitable to the Christian character as born again, is recommended.
Holy conversation among the Gentiles directed.
Subjects exhorted to pay all proper obedience to their civil governors.
Also servants to their masters, and all to be patient, according to the example of the suffering Saviour.
bg: This epistle is addressed to "the strangers scattered abroad", i.e., to the Jews of the Dispersion (the Diaspora).
ch.s: This chapter covers: A temper suitable to the Christian character as born again, is recommended (vv. 1–10); Holy conversation among the Gentiles directed (vv. 11,12); Subjects exhorted to pay all proper obedience to their civil governors (vv. 13–17); Also servants to their masters, and all to be patient, according to the example of the suffering Saviour (vv. 18–25). Places: Sion.
ch.mh: Evil-speaking is a sign of malice and guile in the heart; and hinders our profiting by the word of God.
q: Read verses 1–10 (A temper suitable to the Christian character as born again, is recommended). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 11,12 (Holy conversation among the Gentiles directed), what do you learn about suffering and endurance?
Verse 9 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Exodus 19:5–6. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
Where do you see the theme of sin and repentance in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 Peter?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us not dare to abuse and affront the free grace of God, if we mean to be saved by it; but let all who would be found among those who obtain mercy, walk as his people.
ch.a: Bring a present hardship to God and memorize the key verse as an anchor.

o: The duties of wives and husbands.
And encouraged to patience under persecutions for righteousness' sake, considering that Christ suffered patiently.
bg: This epistle is addressed to "the strangers scattered abroad", i.e., to the Jews of the Dispersion (the Diaspora).

He lived five hundred years, and then there were born unto him three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth (Gen. 5:32). He was a "just man and perfect in his generation," and "walked with God" (comp. Ezek. 14:14, 20).
ch.s: This chapter covers: The duties of wives and husbands (vv. 1–7); Christians exhorted to agree (vv. 8–13); And encouraged to patience under persecutions for righteousness' sake, considering that Christ suffered patiently (vv. 14–22). People named: Abraham, Noah.
ch.mh: The wife must discharge her duty to her own husband, though he obey not the word.
q: Read verses 1–7 (The duties of wives and husbands). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 8–13 (Christians exhorted to agree), what do you learn about suffering and endurance?
Verse 18 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Hebrews 9:28. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Abraham’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of the holy spirit in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 Peter?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us learn to look on the ordinances of God spiritually, and to inquire after the spiritual effect and working of them on our consciences.
ch.a: Bring a present hardship to God and memorize the key verse as an anchor.

o: The consideration of Christ's sufferings is urged for purity and holiness.
And the approaching end of the Jewish state, as a reason for sobriety, watchfulness, and prayer.
Believers encouraged to rejoice and glory in reproaches and sufferings for Christ, and to commit their souls to the care of a faithful God.
bg: This epistle is addressed to "the strangers scattered abroad", i.e., to the Jews of the Dispersion (the Diaspora).
ch.s: This chapter covers: The consideration of Christ's sufferings is urged for purity and holiness (vv. 1–6); And the approaching end of the Jewish state, as a reason for sobriety, watchfulness, and prayer (vv. 7–11); Believers encouraged to rejoice and glory in reproaches and sufferings for Christ, and to commit their souls to the care of a faithful God (vv. 12–19).
ch.mh: The strongest and best arguments against sin, are taken from the sufferings of Christ.
q: Read verses 1–6 (The consideration of Christ's sufferings is urged for purity and holiness). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 7–11 (And the approaching end of the Jewish state, as a reason for sobriety, watchfulness, and prayer), what do you learn about suffering and endurance?
Verse 7 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside James 5:8–9. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
Where do you see the theme of sin and repentance in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 Peter?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: And in all the duties and services of life, we should aim at the glory of God as our chief end.
ch.a: Bring a present hardship to God and memorize the key verse as an anchor.

o: Younger Christians are to submit to their elders, and to yield with humility and patience to God, and to be sober, watchful, and stedfast in faith.
Prayers for their growth and establishment.
bg: This epistle is addressed to "the strangers scattered abroad", i.e., to the Jews of the Dispersion (the Diaspora).
The Babylon mentioned in 1 Pet. 5:13 was not Rome, as some have thought, but the literal city of Babylon, which was inhabited by many Jews at the time Peter wrote.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Elders exhorted and encouraged (vv. 1–4); Younger Christians are to submit to their elders, and to yield with humility and patience to God, and to be sober, watchful, and stedfast in faith (vv. 5–9); Prayers for their growth and establishment (vv. 10–14). People named: Silvanus, Marcus. Places: Babylon.
ch.mh: The apostle Peter does not command, but exhorts.
q: Read verses 1–4 (Elders exhorted and encouraged). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?

In verses 5–9 (Younger Christians are to submit to their elders, and to yield with humility and patience to God, and to be sober, watchful, and stedfast in faith), what do you learn about worship and praise?
Verse 10 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside 2 Corinthians 4:17. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Silvanus’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of the church and fellowship in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 Peter?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: The consideration of what others suffer, is proper to encourage us to bear our share in any affliction; and in whatever form Satan assaults us, or by whatever means, we may know that our brethren experience the same.
ch.a: Write down three things this chapter shows about God and thank Him for each.
